chunks: And say: 'All praise be to God who has neither taken a son nor has a partner in the dominion, nor has He a guardian from ignominy; and exalt Him with great exaltation.'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'And say: All praise be to God' in Surah Al-Isra?
ai.summary: This verse serves as a foundational declaration of Tawhid (monotheism) within Surah Al-Isra, specifically refuting the Christian doctrine of the Sonship and the pagan notion of divine partners. In Shia exegesis, it underscores Allah's absolute self-sufficiency (Al-Ghani) and lack of need for intermediaries, reinforcing the direct relationship between the Creator and the created. The command to 'magnify Him' (Kabbirhu) is often interpreted as an instruction to elevate God in one's heart and speech above all limitations of creation.
